### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Meier-Gorlin syndrome 7  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.484)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-176187)

**Proposed mechanism:** ORC6 (HGNC:8071) —DISRUPTS→ Pre-replication complex assembly (GO:0006272); CDC45 (HGNC:17837) —DISRUPTS→ Pre-replication complex assembly (GO:0006272); Pre-replication complex assembly (GO:0006272) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); Pre-replication complex assembly (GO:0006272) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0002670); Pre-replication complex assembly (GO:0006272) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Pre-replication complex assembly (GO:0006272) —LEADS_TO→ Primordial dwarfism (HP:0009878). Disruption of ORC6 or CDC45 impairs pre-replication complex assembly, leading to a spectrum of developmental abnormalities including microcephaly, skeletal abnormalities, intellectual disability, and primordial dwarfism, common to both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in ORC6 or CDC45 are found at a high frequency (>1%) in healthy individuals within gnomAD, or if experimental evidence demonstrates that disruption of the pre-replication complex assembly does not lead to the observed phenotypes, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: HGNC:8071, HGNC:17837)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ORC6 and CDC45 in DNA replication initiation provides a common molecular target for potential therapeutic interventions aimed at ameliorating the developmental defects seen in both disorders.

#### 2. Meier-Gorlin syndrome 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.478)

Disruptions in ORC4 and ORC6 lead to impaired ORC assembly and function, which is critical for DNA replication initiation. This fundamental defect underlies the shared severe developmental phenotypes observed in both diseases, including microcephaly, intellectual disability, short stature, and developmental delay.

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be falsified if genetic studies reveal that disease A is caused by a gain-of-function mutation in ORC4/ORC6, or if disease B is caused by a mutation in an entirely unrelated pathway that does not converge on DNA replication initiation or cell cycle control. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD within the coding regions of ORC4 or ORC6 that are not associated with either phenotype would weaken the direct causal link but not necessarily falsify the mechanistic overlap at the pathway level.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the ORC complex in both diseases suggests that therapeutic strategies aimed at supporting DNA replication fidelity or cell cycle progression could potentially benefit patients with either condition. This highlights a common vulnerability in the cellular machinery underlying these distinct rare diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in ORC6 or RFC4 with a clear dominant-negative or gain-of-function effect in patient-derived cells would falsify this haploinsufficiency hypothesis. **Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathways of DNA replication initiation and nucleotide biosynthesis could reveal common therapeutic targets for MONDO:0013430 and Morimoto-Ryu-Malicdan neuromuscular syndrome, potentially enabling the development of treatments that address the underlying molecular defects affecting neuronal development and function.

#### 6. pulmonary fibrosis and/or bone marrow failure, telomere-related, 6  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.424)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-176187)

**Proposed mechanism:** ORC6 (HGNC:8059) —DISRUPTS→ Origin recognition complex assembly (GO:0006277); Origin recognition complex assembly (GO:0006277) —LEADS_TO→ DNA replication checkpoint (GO:0007274); DNA replication checkpoint (GO:0007274) —LEADS_TO→ Pulmonary fibrosis (HP:0002099); RPA1 (HGNC:10102) —DISRUPTS→ DNA replication initiation (GO:0006260); DNA replication initiation (GO:0006260) —LEADS_TO→ DNA replication checkpoint (GO:0007274); DNA replication checkpoint (GO:0007274) —LEADS_TO→ Bone marrow failure (HP:0011540). Loss-of-function mutations in ORC6 disrupt the origin recognition complex assembly, which is essential for initiating DNA replication and activating the DNA replication checkpoint. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in RPA1 impair DNA replication itself, also leading to activation of the DNA replication checkpoint. Dysregulation of the DNA replication checkpoint contributes to the pathogenesis of both pulmonary fibrosis and bone marrow failure.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of genetic variants in ORC6 or RPA1 in individuals diagnosed with either MONDO:0013430 or MONDO:0030690, respectively, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if these genes were shown to be pathogenic only in gain-of-function manner for either disease, this would also falsify the proposed loss-of-function overlap.

**Why it matters:** Identifying the shared role of the DNA replication checkpoint pathway and its key components (ORC6, RPA1) in both diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies that modulate this pathway for the treatment of both MONDO:0013430 and MONDO:0030690.
